subtopics.name: Characteristics of Living Things
objectives: Differentiate between the characteristics of living and non-living things.
Recall the seven life processes (MRS GREN).
Distinguish between aerobic and anaerobic respiration.
Distinguish between autotrophic and heterotrophic nutrition.

subtopics.name: The Cell — Basic Unit of Life
objectives: Identify the structures of plant and animal cells.
Analyse the functions of cell components.
Compare and contrast plant and animal cells.
State the cell theory and the scientists associated with it.

subtopics.name: Organisation and Classification
objectives: Trace the levels of organisation: Cell, Tissue, Organ, System, Organism.
Distinguish between unicellular and multicellular organisms.
Classify organisms into the five kingdoms.
Explain why viruses are considered acellular.

subtopics.name: Evolution of Plants
objectives: Trace the evolutionary sequence of plants: Thallophyta → Bryophyta → Pteridophyta → Spermatophyta.
Distinguish features of Gymnosperms and Angiosperms.
Describe the features of Monera, Protista, and Fungi.
Account for the transition from aquatic to terrestrial plants.

subtopics.name: Evolution of Animals — Invertebrates
objectives: Trace the advancement of invertebrate animals.
Identify distinguishing features of each invertebrate phylum.
Determine the economic importance of insects.
State the correct evolutionary sequence of invertebrates.

subtopics.name: Evolution of Animals — Vertebrates
objectives: Trace the advancement of multicellular animals from fish to mammals.
Compare features of vertebrate classes.
Describe the frog life cycle as evidence of transition from water to land.
Determine the economic importance of vertebrates.

subtopics.name: Structural Adaptations
objectives: Describe how structures adapt organisms to their environment.
Explain adaptations for obtaining food (bird beaks, insect mouthparts).
Explain adaptations for protection and defence (camouflage, spines).
Describe adaptations for water conservation and thermoregulation.

subtopics.name: Functional Adaptations
objectives: Describe physiological adaptations of desert animals.
Explain water conservation mechanisms in animals.
Describe venom production and its functions in snakes.

subtopics.name: Behavioural Adaptations
objectives: Categorise countershading in fish, toads, and snakes.
Explain warning colouration and its function.
Differentiate castes in termite colonies and their roles.
Account for basking in lizards, hibernation, and aestivation.

topics.name: Internal Structure of a Flowering Plant

subtopics.name: Root, Stem and Leaf Structure
objectives: Identify transverse sections of root, stem, and leaf.
Relate structure to function in plant organs.
Identify supporting tissues: collenchyma, sclerenchyma, xylem, phloem fibres.
Describe the distribution of supporting tissues in root, stem, and leaf.

subtopics.name: Internal Structure of a Mammal
objectives: Examine the arrangement of mammalian internal organs.
Describe the position and appearance of digestive, reproductive, and excretory organs.

subtopics.name: Modes of Nutrition
objectives: Compare autotrophic and heterotrophic modes of nutrition.
Provide examples of photosynthetic and chemosynthetic nutrition.
Differentiate holozoic, parasitic, saprophytic, and symbiotic nutrition.

subtopics.name: Plant Nutrition
objectives: Describe photosynthesis and the conditions required.
Identify macro and micro-nutrient requirements in plants.
State the role of mineral salts in plant growth.

subtopics.name: Animal Nutrition
objectives: Identify the six classes of food substances and their functions.
Perform food tests for starch, reducing sugar, protein, and fat.
Describe the structure and functions of mammalian teeth.
Describe digestion, absorption, and assimilation in the alimentary canal.

subtopics.name: Transport in Plants
objectives: Describe the process of osmosis and its role in plants.
Explain the movement of water through xylem vessels.
Describe the translocation of food in phloem.

subtopics.name: Transport in Animals
objectives: Describe the composition and functions of blood.
Trace the pathway of blood through the heart and lungs.
Compare open and closed circulatory systems.
Describe the lymphatic system.

subtopics.name: Types of Respiration
objectives: Differentiate aerobic from anaerobic respiration.
Write equations for aerobic and anaerobic respiration.
Describe the role of ATP in energy transfer.
Explain the respiratory quotient (RQ).

subtopics.name: Respiratory Systems
objectives: Describe the mechanism of breathing in mammals.
Compare respiratory surfaces in fish, insects, and mammals.
Describe gaseous exchange in plants and animals.

subtopics.name: Excretion in Plants
objectives: Identify excretory products in plants.
Describe how plants remove carbon dioxide and oxygen.

subtopics.name: Excretion in Animals
objectives: Describe the structure and function of the mammalian kidney.
Explain the process of urine formation (filtration, reabsorption, secretion).
Compare excretory products in different organisms (urea, uric acid, ammonia).
Describe the role of the skin and lungs in excretion.

subtopics.name: Support in Plants
objectives: Describe mechanisms of support in herbaceous and woody plants.
Explain the role of turgidity in plant support.
Identify supporting tissues in plants.

subtopics.name: Support and Movement in Animals
objectives: Describe the structure of the mammalian skeleton.
Explain the mechanism of muscle contraction.
Compare endoskeleton, exoskeleton, and hydrostatic skeleton.
Describe the structure of synovial joints.

subtopics.name: Reproduction in Plants
objectives: Describe sexual and asexual reproduction in plants.
Identify the parts of a flower and their functions.
Describe pollination, fertilisation, and seed dispersal.
Describe vegetative propagation methods.

subtopics.name: Reproduction in Animals
objectives: Compare asexual and sexual reproduction in animals.
Describe the human reproductive system (male and female).
Explain fertilisation, pregnancy, and birth.
Describe metamorphosis in insects and frogs.

subtopics.name: Growth and Development
objectives: Define growth and state its characteristics.
Describe the germination of seeds.
Draw growth curves (sigmoid, growth rate curves).
Describe growth in plants and animals.

subtopics.name: Metamorphosis, Regeneration, and Secondary Growth
objectives: Distinguish between epigeal and hypogeal germination.
Explain complete and incomplete metamorphosis in insects.
Describe secondary growth in dicotyledonous plants.
Explain the role of meristems in plant growth.

subtopics.name: The Nervous System
objectives: Describe the structure and functions of neurons.
Explain reflex action and the reflex arc.
Describe the structure of the brain and spinal cord.
Describe the sense organs and their functions.

subtopics.name: Hormonal Co-ordination
objectives: Describe the endocrine glands and the hormones they produce.
Explain the effects of hormones on growth, reproduction, and metabolism.
Compare nervous and hormonal control.

subtopics.name: Factors Affecting Distribution of Organisms
objectives: Identify abiotic and biotic factors affecting distribution.
Describe how temperature, light, humidity, and soil affect organisms.
Explain the concept of the ecological niche.

subtopics.name: Symbiotic Interactions
objectives: Define symbiosis, mutualism, commensalism, and parasitism.
Give examples of each type of interaction.
Describe predator-prey relationships and competition.

subtopics.name: Natural Habitats and Biomes
objectives: Describe the features of aquatic and terrestrial habitats.
Identify Nigerian biomes: forest, savanna, Sahel.
Describe food chains, food webs, and energy flow.
Explain biogeochemical cycles: carbon, nitrogen, water cycles.

subtopics.name: Ecology of Populations
objectives: Define population and describe factors affecting population size.
Describe growth curves and limiting factors.
Explain conservation of natural resources.
Describe the effects of pollution on the environment.

subtopics.name: Heredity and Variation
objectives: Define genetics, gene, allele, genotype, and phenotype.
Explain Mendel's laws of inheritance.
Solve monohybrid and dihybrid cross problems.
Explain sex determination and sex-linked characteristics.

subtopics.name: Application of Genetics
objectives: Describe mutations and their causes.
Explain variation (continuous and discontinuous).
Describe the significance of variation in evolution.
Discuss the application of genetics in agriculture and medicine.
